messages:
Marco: Hey team! A few onboarding/payroll/benefits items I need help with. Sorry for the barrage.
Marco: 1) I uploaded my W-4 but Workday still shows "pending". Will that block taxes on my next paycheck?
Marco: 2) My offer had a $2k sign-on bonus line; I don't see it on my stub. Is that a payroll timing thing or a separate payment?
Marco: 3) I submitted receipts for moving boxes and a temporary storage locker. Do those go through Expensify or a special relocation flow?
Marco: 4) PTO question: I started mid-quarter; do floating holidays get prorated or do I get the full bank?
benefits-bot: Welcome Marco! Quick links: onboarding checklist https://redwood.example/onboard, payroll checklist https://payroll.redwood.example/onboard, benefits portal https://benefits.redwood.example (SSO).
Maya (People Ops): Hey Marco �Hello and congrats! Short answers up front: W-4 pending shouldn't block payroll but may default withholding to single/0 until processed. We'll confirm. Sign-on bonus often pays on a scheduled bonus run; depends on how it was coded (payroll stipend vs one-time bonus). Relocation/expenses usually go to Expensify unless your offer specifically says "paid as payroll." Holidays: company observed holidays are granted to all employees (not prorated). Floating days are prorated based on hire date per the PTO policy.
Lina (Payroll): Hi Marco �I can check W-4 status. If Workday shows pending it means the docs haven't hit payroll queue before cutoff; taxes default to federal withholding at single with 0 unless we have another code. If you want to avoid the default, send me a DM with the W-4 file and I'll push it for the next cycle.
Lina (Payroll): Regarding the sign-on bonus: if Recruiting marked it as a "Signing Bonus" it will hit the bonus payroll run which is monthly on the 2nd Friday of the month. If it's coded as a relocation/stipend it could appear sooner as stipend code. Tagging @Jamal to confirm coding for your offer.
Jamal (Finance): Marco �I pulled your offer. The $2,000 is coded as "Sign-On Bonus - One-time" and is queued for the next bonus run (2nd Fri). It also has a 30-day clawback clause in the offer, so Payroll withheld it from the regular run pending final eligibility. We'll process on the bonus date and you should see it as a separate line item.
Marco: Thanks �Jamal. Good to know. For the moving expenses: receipts are primarily boxes + storage under $500 total. Recruiter told me to just expense them.
Tess (Recruiting): Marco �I asked Recruiting Ops to approve those. If it's under the relocation cap and recruiter approved, Expensify with tag "Relocation-Receipts" is fine. Include the recruiting approval email as an attachment so Finance doesn't hold it.
Marco: Great. Any expected timeline for reimbursement once I submit?
Jamal (Finance): Once Expensify is approved we process within one reimburse cycle (7 business days typical). If we need additional documentation it'll be held and we'll ping you. Make sure receipts are PDF or clear photos and line-itemized when possible.
Marco: PTO thing: I had two floating holidays in offer. Do those show up immediately or pro-rated?
Maya (People Ops): If your offer explicitly lists floating holidays, those are credited per the offer and will be visible in Workday under Time Off > Balances within 1 pay cycle. Standard floating holidays for new hires are prorated unless called out in the offer.
Marco: Helpful. One more: I added my spouse as a dependent in benefits but got an upload request for documentation. I uploaded the marriage cert—how long to verify?
Maya (People Ops): Benefits team usually verifies docs within 3 business days. If status is still "Needs Review" after 72 hours tag this thread and I'll expedite. If anything's missing the portal lists required docs; you have 30 days to submit.
Lina (Payroll): Also heads up: dependent changes can affect your tax withholdings for benefits pre-tax premiums; once verified payroll will reflect any changes in the next cycle.
Marco: Appreciate it. Last tiny one: I filled out 401(k) enrollment but it asked about Roth vs Traditional employer match. Which do you recommend for new hires? :)
Maya (People Ops): We don't give financial advice, but quick facts: employer match applies the same irrespective of Roth vs Traditional; Roth defers tax on contributions now and gives tax-free distributions later. You can change deferral elections anytime via Workday > Benefits > Retirement. We also have a recorded session with our advisor on the intranet: https://handbook.redwood.example/401k-guide.
Marco: Perfect. I'll submit Expensify now and ping if W-4 stays pending. Thanks everyone for the rapid replies! :thumbsup:
Maya (People Ops): Welcome aboard Marco! Tag us if anything hangs up and we'll sort it. :tada:
